topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening subtopic introduces the lecturer, sets the context within the cancer lecture series, and outlines the primary learning objectives regarding cancer etiology and carcinogens.

topics.label: Etiology of Cancer and Epidemiological Patterns
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the fundamental nature of cancer as a multi-factorial evolutionary process driven by intrinsic cellular errors, genetic predispositions, and geographically variable environmental exposures.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Carcinogenic Agents and Tumor Promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics analyze the biological and chemical mechanisms by which pathogens, environmental chemicals, radiation, metabolic activation, and tumor promoters drive malignant transformation and clonal outgrowth.

topics.label: Methodologies for Assessing and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the scientific approaches, tools, and challenges involved in identifying carcinogens, ranging from mutational signature analysis and biobank epidemiology to in vivo toxicology and in vitro assays.
